name: Khusnutdinov-Sushkov 2002 short-throat self-consistent wormhole

source.located: N.R. Khusnutdinov & S.V. Sushkov, 'Ground state energy in a wormhole space-time', arXiv:hep-th/0202068, Phys. Rev. D 65, 084028 (15 April 2002)
source.via: Paper body NOT read: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries / get_paper_content / discover_papers all returned 'assistant quota exceeded' (3 attempts); arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org, alphaxiv.org, journals.aps.org, osti.gov, kpfu.ru, inspirehep, semanticscholar all EGRESS_BLOCKED (403). What was read: the abstract as excerpted by WebSearch (three independent queries returned the same abstract sentences, consistent with the APS/OSTI/ResearchGate abstract pages), and the short-throat metric r = a + |rho|, R = -8 delta(rho)/a as restated in WebSearch excerpts of arXiv:1003.0344 (vacuum polarization of a massive scalar in a wormhole spacetime) and related Khusnutdinov-lineage papers. No equation, table or section of the KS body was seen.

published_statement: Abstract (as excerpted): 'The ground state energy of the massive scalar field with non-conformal coupling xi on the short-throat flat-space wormhole background is calculated by using zeta renormalization approach. ... We show that the stable configuration of wormholes can exist for xi > 0.123. In particular case of massive conformal scalar field with xi = 1/6, the radius of throat of stable wormhole a ~ 0.16/m. The self-consistent wormhole has the radius of throat a ~ 0.0141 l_P and the mass of scalar boson m ~ 11.35 m_P (l_P and m_P are the Planck length and mass, respectively).'
published_hypotheses: Background: short-throat flat-space wormhole -- two copies of Minkowski space with balls excised and boundaries identified; r = a + |rho|, flat for rho != 0, curvature concentrated at the throat (R = -8 delta(rho)/a, per later restatement)
Field: a single massive scalar field, mass m, with non-conformal coupling xi to curvature
Quantity: ground-state (vacuum / Casimir-type) energy, zeta-function renormalisation, with heat-kernel coefficients
Stability = the ground-state energy as a function of a has a minimum; exists only for xi > 0.123
'Self-consistent' wormhole: an additional condition (NOT READ here -- its exact form is in the unread body) that fixes m ~ 11.35 m_P and hence a ~ 0.0141 l_P
Implicit: semiclassical treatment (quantised matter on a classical geometry), one scalar only, no graviton loop; result sits at a < l_P and m > m_P
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (tacit) SMOOTHNESS AT THE THROAT -- throatmass.py:134-136 and the --selftest cross-check at throatmass.py:356-362 assign KS 'm = r_0/2 > 0 at the throat' via the smooth-throat substitution r' = 0. In KS's geometry r' jumps from -1 to +1 at rho = 0 (r'' = 2 delta(rho)); the Misner-Sharp mass is exactly 0 on both flat sides and undefined at the throat itself. m = a/2 at the throat is the limit of every smooth even regularisation with |r'| <= 1 (computed), not a quantity of KS's geometry. The sign conclusion the tree draws (no m < 0; 'm < 0 reported' = False) survives -- m = 0 off-throat, m >= 0 under every such regularisation, ADM mass 0 on each side -- but the VALUE r_0/2 is regularisation-defined for this family, and the throatmass.py:24-28 SERIES_RESULT premise (finite r''(0)) fails for it.

DROPPED: the meaning of 'self-consistent' -- throatmass.py:122-130 lists KS among 'self-consistent solution families' beside HPS gr-qc/9701064 (which solves local semiclassical Einstein equations). KS's exterior is exactly flat, G_mu_nu = 0 for rho != 0, so the geometry is a solution of the LOCAL semiclassical equations off the throat only if <T_mu_nu>_ren vanishes there; the paper's self-consistency condition fixes one number (m ~ 11.35 m_P) and so appears to be a global/energy condition, not the local equations. The exact condition is NOT READ -- recorded as an unverified drift, not a finding.

Does not move the tree's use: KS is not the largest throat (HPS 300 l_P sets LARGEST_THROAT_M, throatmass.py:193-194).

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (24 checks). (A) 0.16/11.35 = 0.014096916 -> 0.0141: the abstract's xi = 1/6 stable radius a = 0.16/m at m = 11.35 m_P reproduces a = 0.0141 l_P. (B) r = a + |rho|: Misner-Sharp m = (r/2)(1 - r'^2) = 0 exactly on both sides. (C) two smooth even regularisations (a + sqrt(rho^2+eps^2) - eps; a + eps ln cosh(rho/eps)): r'(0) = 0, m(0) = a/2 exactly, m >= 0 on a numeric grid. (D) shell energy int rho_E 4 pi r^2 dl -> -1.99956 / -1.99961 (a = 1, eps = 1e-3) i.e. -2a, sigma = -1/(2 pi a); int R drho -> -7.989 / -7.994 vs the restated -8/a; 3-curvature formula R = -2(2 r r'' + r'^2 - 1)/r^2 derived from the metric by sympy. (E) r''(0) = 1/eps -> infinity: the tree's series premise fails for this family.

lacked_data: KS 2002 is a pure one-loop QFT-on-fixed-background computation; its only numerical inputs are the Planck units (and xi, m as parameters). No measurement later arrived that bears on it: G and hbar have not moved materially (CODATA 2018/2022 G = 6.67430e-11), and the output (a ~ 0.0141 l_P, m ~ 11.35 m_P) lies where no data exists or is foreseeably obtainable. What the authors lacked is theoretical, not data: graviton loops (added by Garattini 2005), back-reaction beyond the thin-shell ansatz, and a trustworthy theory at a < l_P. Evidence either way: having CODATA 2022 moves the metre value by ~1e-4 relative and changes no conclusion; nothing supports M's hypothesis for this result, and nothing refutes it -- the regime is simply outside the reach of data.
grade_evidence: The number the tree seats (r_0 = 0.0141 l_P, xi = 1/6) matches the abstract and is arithmetically consistent with its a = 0.16/m at m = 11.35 m_P (computed). The tree's per-family sign 'm < 0 reported: False' survives (computed: Misner-Sharp m = 0 on both flat sides; m >= 0 and m(0) = a/2 under every tested smooth even regularisation; ADM mass 0). NARROWED because the tree's statement 'm = r_0/2 > 0 at the throat' and its --selftest cross-check use the smooth-throat substitution r' = 0, a hypothesis KS's thin-shell geometry does not satisfy (r' jumps -1 -> +1, r''(0) -> infinity; m at the throat is regularisation-defined), and because the tree drops the sub-Planckian/trans-Planckian regime and xi > 0.123. A second possible narrowing -- that KS's 'self-consistent' is a global condition, not a solution of the local semiclassical equations like HPS -- is supported by the flat exterior (G_mu_nu = 0 off the throat) but the paper's condition was NOT READ, so it is recorded as OPEN inside this grade, not counted as evidence. No misprint or refutation was found; nothing is WRONG. The grade rests on the abstract (via search excerpt) and a restated metric: the KS body was unreadable here (alphaXiv quota; arXiv/APS egress-blocked).
what_would_change_the_grade: Reading the KS body (hep-th/0202068) at source: (i) if its metric is a smooth throat rather than r = a + |rho| the smoothness drift disappears (-> STANDS on the sign and value); (ii) if its self-consistency condition is the local semiclassical Einstein equation with <T_mu_nu>_ren = 0 off the throat, the 'self-consistent family' classification stands; if it is a global energy balance, the tree's grouping of KS with HPS narrows further; (iii) if the 0.0141 l_P figure is NOT the xi = 1/6 case, the tree's label 'xi = 1/6 minimum' becomes a discrepancy (not a refutation).
